card.name: Auxiliary 'have/has' before 'been reported'
card.fires_on: The helper word 'have' or 'has' right after a list of reactions or events, just before 'been reported' or 'occurred'. Also fires on a dose unit or noun that ends a clause of reported cases.

modes.label: have/has before reported
modes.description: The helper verb follows a reaction or drug subject and leads into 'been reported' or 'occurred'.
modes.example: Reversal of such responses with flumazenil<< has>> been reported in pediatric patients.

modes.label: Dose or noun ending a subject
modes.description: A unit or noun closes the subject, just before 'have been administered' or 'have occurred'.
modes.example: total daily intravenous doses as large as 252<< mg>> have been inadvertently administered without significant adverse events

card.writes: It favors words that introduce a case or experience, such as 'instance', 'example', 'case', 'successfully', and 'has been'.
card.plain: It marks the spot where a label says that an effect 'has been reported' or 'has occurred'.
